# Grading and Condition

American coins are graded on the 70-point Sheldon scale, which runs
from Poor-1 to Mint State 70. The scale was devised by William Sheldon
in 1949, originally as a pricing formula for large cents, and was
adopted as a pure condition scale by the grading services in the 1980s.

Grades of MS-60 and above denote Mint State — no wear from circulation,
though bag marks and weak strikes still separate an MS-60 from an
MS-65. Third-party certification by PCGS or NGC, both founded in the
mid-1980s, made sight-unseen trading possible and underpins the modern
auction market.

A single grade point at the top of the scale can multiply price several
times over, which is why crossover and regrade submissions are a
permanent feature of the hobby.
